Summary: The Trinity teaches that God is one in essence and three in Persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Each Person is fully God, distinct from the others, and eternally united, and Christians worship one God, not three gods.
HistoricalDevelopment: Affirmed against Arianism at the Council of Nicaea in AD 325 and clarified at Constantinople in AD 381, the doctrine was expressed in the Nicene Creed and defended by Athanasius and the Cappadocian Fathers.
Interpretations: All historic Christian traditions affirm the Trinity, though they differ in explaining the procession of the Spirit, including the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic debate over the filioque clause.
RelatedTopics: God; Jesus Christ; Holy Spirit; Monotheism
RelatedPeople: Athanasius; Augustine; Basil of Caesarea; Aquinas
